frictionSummary: Self-serve app creation; public distribution via the App Directory needs review.
prerequisites: A Slack workspace you can create apps in (api.slack.com/apps)
A clear list of the minimum scopes your app actually needs — Slack's reviewers check for least-privilege requests
If targeting the App Directory: a demo video of the full install/OAuth/uninstall flow, submitted 2-3 weeks ahead of launch

steps.title: Create the app
steps.body: api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → From scratch. Pick the workspace to develop against.

steps.title: Add OAuth scopes
steps.body: Under OAuth & Permissions, add Bot Token Scopes (and User Token Scopes if needed). Slack separates scopes granted at install from ones requested later, but review criteria apply to both.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL and install to your workspace
steps.body: Add your redirect URL under OAuth & Permissions, then install the app to your own workspace to test immediately — no review needed for internal use.
steps.codeSnippet:
curl -X POST https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET \
  -d code=THE_AUTH_CODE \
  -d redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI

steps.title: Submit to the App Directory only if you need public distribution
steps.body: Listing in the App Directory requires a formal review: justify every requested scope, provide a demo video of install → OAuth → functionality → uninstall, and submit weeks ahead of your target launch date. You can distribute an app outside the Directory with no review at all.

scopes.grants: View basic information about public channels

approval.expectedWait: None for internal/direct install; review required only for App Directory listing
approval.notes: Doc-sourced from Slack's App Directory Partner Submission Guide and App Review Guide. Review centers on scope justification and a working demo video; apps not seeking Directory listing can be installed and used with no review step.

gotchas: Scopes requested beyond the minimum trigger extra scrutiny — justify every scope in the submission, not just list them
Broad/sensitive scopes (like *:history) require showing your data handling and retention practices
Once an app is published to the Directory, changing scopes or config means resubmitting for review — the older version stays live until the new one is approved
App Directory submissions need lead time: 3 weeks for new apps, 2 weeks for updates to already-listed apps
You don't need the App Directory at all if you're distributing the app yourself (e.g. an internal tool or a direct-install link)

do: Create /api/auth/slack/callback — exchanges the code at https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access
Add placeholder env vars: SLACK_CLIENT_ID, SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, SLACK_REDIRECT_URI
Wire up a "Add to Slack" button redirecting to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with only the scopes actually used
Keep the scope list minimal and documented — it makes a future App Directory submission much faster
dont: Request broad scopes like channels:history speculatively — each one needs a justification if you ever submit for Directory review
Submit to the App Directory without the developer's go-ahead — it starts a real review clock and needs a demo video
Enter the real client secret or signing secret anywhere — leave them as env placeholders
